A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MM-UPT, with matching methods and original experiments despite the changed title. The main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MM-UPT evaluations, synthetic-data experiments, backbone comparisons, training dynamics and a failure-case experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds pass@10, visual-question-answering generalization and text-only mathematical reasoning results.

M1.justification: The GRPO objective, majority-vote pseudo-rewards and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Both synthetic-data strategies already appeared in v1 Section 4.3 and are reorganized into v2 Section 3.3. The language-model experiment applies the same self-rewarding procedure without a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Appendices B.2–B.3 add ChartQA and IconQA evaluations and extend the work to text-only mathematical reasoning, training on DAPO-17K and evaluating on MATH and Omni-MATH. This substantially broadens the evaluated domains while retaining the original visual-mathematics coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparison methods: supervised GRPO, rejection SFT, SRLM, LMSI, Genixer and STIC. The added experiments reuse comparisons against the underlying base model and supervised GRPO; the language experiment changes the backbone, without introducing a new competing training method.

E3.justification: v2 adds pass@10 evaluation in Table 5 and a Qwen2.5-MATH-7B configuration for the new language experiment. Previously specified training settings and benchmark judging remain unchanged. The newly stated rollout temperature and group size are disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments used different settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds a diagnostic comparison testing whether improved single-response accuracy sacrifices success across multiple responses. Appendix B.2 tests whether mathematical post-training harms broader visual-question-answering performance. These materially extend the analysis of limitations and generalization. Existing backbone ablations, synthetic examples, ThinkLite failure results and training dynamics are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added pass@10 evaluation concerns multiple generated responses, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figure 2 retain their results. New Table 5 reports average pass@10 of 0.8003 for the base model, 0.7250 for MM-UPT and 0.7634 for supervised GRPO. New base-versus-UPT comparisons report ChartQA 71.96→77.48 and IconQA 54.20→56.55 in Table 6, and MATH 51.20→75.80 and Omni-MATH 18.09→32.72 in Table 7. These are additional findings, not revised scores for the original experiments.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, GRPO and majority-voting equations, binomial justification and appendix filtering equations are unchanged. The semantic-entropy definition moves with the training-dynamics analysis to Appendix B.1. The three-stage framing introduces no new mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: v2 elevates v1's recommendation to refine an already supervised model into an explicit SFT–RL–UPT paradigm, claiming priority in formalizing this three-stage arrangement. This refines the headline contribution, while the central claims about majority-vote self-improvement and synthetic-data effectiveness remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 explains how consensus rewards can suppress occasionally correct minority responses and discusses training-versus-inference cost trade-offs. Section 4.4 explicitly interprets retained results as compatibility with prior supervised GRPO, while Appendices B.2–B.3 discuss transfer and language-only applicability. These substantially expand the interpretation beyond v1's existing warning about insufficient prior competence.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies rollout temperature 0.7 and one rollout group of size 10 per data point per episode. Baseline implementation details, benchmark judging, code access and hardware information remain unchanged; compute resources move from Appendix B to C.

R1.justification: The main distinction from SFT/DPO-based self-improvement remains. v2 adds qualifications about STIC/SENA's perceptual focus, relates the diversity finding to Yue et al.'s RL-capacity study, and adds references supporting the new benchmarks and language experiment. Some background references, including BLIP-2 and Visual Sketchpad, are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around three-stage post-training. Synthetic-data descriptions move into a dedicated methods subsection, experimental scenarios receive explicit labels, and training dynamics move to the appendix while trade-offs receive a main-text subsection. This is substantial narrative restructuring despite the stable algorithm.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact results tables, relocates Figure 2 to the appendix, and updates scenario labels, the algorithm caption and display spacing. The existing schematic, plots, synthetic examples and original tables retain their basic visual organization.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more balanced assessment: Table 5 exposes reduced multi-response success that v1 did not quantify, and Tables 6–7 add evidence about broader applicability. Newly disclosed rollout settings also improve reproducibility. These are useful gains, although sparse protocol details for the added evaluations limit the strength of the expanded conclusions; the stronger three-stage framing does not itself establish an additional scientific advance.
